newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada T-bills open little changed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Canada T-bills open little changed in quiet trade.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened little changed in quiet trade on Wednesday, with account buying subdued and a squeeze affecting the six-month area of the curve, dealers said.

"It's a very strange market today. You have serious technical distortions in some areas of the curve," said Walter Posiewko, a money market trader with Royal Bank Investment Management. "I don't think you're seeing any kind of huge buying from accounts."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill traded with a yield of 3.24 percent, unchanged from Tuesday's close.
Analysts said the the threat of a U.S. rate hike in May and its possible impact on the Canadian dollar continues to weigh on the money market and keep many accounts on the sidelines.
"I think a lot of end-buyers, especially domestic accounts have been very much on the sidelines throughout all this," said a T-bill dealer with one bank-owned brokerage.
In the interim, the Canadian T-bill yield curve is being slightly distorted by a squeeze in six-month cash bill which originated last week, dealers said.
"Sixes (cash bills) are totally skewed. There seems to be a squeeze that materialized last week that's continuing right through here and is now spilling over into WI sixes," said Posiewko.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill softened to yield 3.63 percent from 3.60 percent on Tuesday. The one-year when-issued T-bill softened to yield 4.39 percent from 4.33 percent.
The call loan rate traded at 3.10 percent, in the upper half of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
